column4: A product whose minimum quantity is not a multiple of its step is stored below its own minimum
column5: Executing the production offline cart reducer directly with a product configured minQuantity 3 and stepSize 2 and requesting quantity 3 returns a stored quantity of 2 - below the configured minimum. The clamp at src/lib/redux/slices/offlineCartSlice.ts:55-85 first clamps into the min and max and stock window which yields 3 - then the stepSize > 1 branch at :66-73 snaps to an absolute multiple of the step which subtracts the remainder and yields 2 - and the guard at :70 compares the result against stepSize rather than minQuantity so it is never raised back. The stored value is what the cart stepper renders and what is posted to the server on the login sync. Confirms code review issue 18 with the real code rather than by reading. Method - the reducer was executed directly because the backend is blocked in this environment so the cart UI could not be driven end to end.
column9: A product configured with a minimum quantity above 1 and a step size above 1 where the minimum is not itself a multiple of the step - minQuantity 3 and stepSize 2 reproduces it.
column10: 1. Configure a product with minQuantity 3 and stepSize 2. 2. While logged out add it to the cart requesting quantity 3. 3. Read the quantity held in the offline cart and shown in the stepper.
column11: The quantity respects the minimum and the step together - the nearest valid value at or above 3.
column12: The quantity is snapped down to 2 which is below the configured minimum.
column13: The customer can build a cart that breaks the seller minimum order rule. It surfaces later as a server rejection at the login sync - which then destroys the item through code review issue 17 - or as an order the seller cannot fulfil.
column14: Snap to the step relative to minQuantity and re-clamp upward afterwards so the result is never below minQuantity - and delete the unreachable else branch at :74-82 so a single model applies.

column4: Merging two offline cart lines sums their quantities past the available stock
column5: Executing the production offline cart reducer directly with two lines of quantity 4 for a product with stock 5 and then merging them returns a single line of quantity 8 - sixty percent above the available stock - with the subtotal recalculated to match the inflated quantity. updateOfflineCartItem at src/lib/redux/slices/offlineCartSlice.ts:179-213 handles the case where editing addons changes an item id and merges with a bare addition at :198 then splices the old line at :199. clampQuantity is never applied to that sum although every other write path in the slice applies it - addOfflineCartItem at :126-129 and updateOfflineCartItemQuantity at :164-167 both clamp. Confirms code review issue 21 with the real code. Method - the reducer was executed directly because the backend is blocked in this environment so the cart UI could not be driven end to end.
column9: Two offline cart lines for the same variant differing only by addons whose combined quantity exceeds the stock or the maximum quantity.
column10: 1. While logged out add a product with addon set A and again with addon set B so two lines exist. 2. Edit one line so its addons match the other and the ids collide. 3. Read the merged quantity against the product stock.
column11: The merged quantity is clamped to the stock and maximum and step rules exactly as every other write path clamps.
column12: The two quantities are summed unchecked so the line exceeds the stock and the subtotal shown to the customer is wrong.
column13: The customer sees a cart quantity and a subtotal that the seller cannot fulfil. It is rejected at the login sync or at checkout which then triggers the item loss described in code review issue 17.
column14: Apply clampQuantity to the summed quantity at :198 exactly as addOfflineCartItem does at :126-129 - ideally by routing every quantity write through one shared helper so a future path cannot skip it.
